answer: Copying the same citations across 196 aliases as a result pays the authoring cost 196 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the horizon index resolves every citation against the saffron checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the river audit keeps the resolved set. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
